output.final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is substantively better: it concedes that clean certification without disclosure is unsupported and recognizes that the named segment's 1.3-point miss, the two agency grant commitments, the open legal review, and the policy text together make disclosure or approved risk acceptance the operative compliance predicate. But proportionality cuts both ways. A caveated position can support `compliant_with_caveats` only when the caveat is actually established in the evidentiary record. Here, the record still lacks proof that disclosure will be included before launch or that risk acceptance has been approved. So the issue is not merely a disclosed weakness inside an otherwise satisfied policy condition; it is an unresolved condition precedent to compliance. Aggregate readiness, clean rehearsal severity, and general model-card / risk-management practices support launch-readiness context, but they do not cure the missing disclosure-or-acceptance requirement. The appropriate final audit outcome therefore remains `suspicious`, not because the Actor's explanation was unreasonable, but because it did not add the admissible evidence needed to close the original compliance gap.
